slides.title: Raise prices in 2027 — but only where Palisade has pricing power

paragraphs.text: Raise prices in 2027 — but only where Palisade has pricing power
Recommendation on the 2027 pricing plan: should Palisade raise prices while churn is rising, and if so, how?
CEO and leadership team  |  Pricing decision meeting, December 2026
Prepared from the 2026 briefing pack only (synthetic benchmark data); all figures $M ARR unless stated

slides.title: Yes, raise prices in 2027 by segment: +10% for mid-market and enterprise, hold SMB until a test reads out, and retain the promo cohort without a price rise

paragraphs.text: Yes, raise prices in 2027 by segment: +10% for mid-market and enterprise, hold SMB until a test reads out, and retain the promo cohort without a price rise

Answer: The recommended plan adds about $3.0M of net ARR in 2027, and up to $0.5M more if the SMB test passes. It gives the same ~$2.0M as the CFO's flat +12% in the downside case and less SMB risk. No pricing option reaches the 15% growth target on its own; new customers must supply the last ~$1.9M.
Churn is rising because of one cohort, not because customers broadly reject the price

Core SMB churn went from 2.0% to only 2.1% a month. The 2,100 customers from the 2025 promotion churn at ~4.9% a month and make up 56% of SMB churners. Better onboarding explains only ~30% of their excess churn; the rest is a reaction to the discount ending.
Mid-market and enterprise can take a price rise; SMB has not shown it can

Mid-market: a +10% test had no significant effect on conversion (23.1% vs 23.6%), churn is 0.8% a month and NRR is 112%. Enterprise: 0.2% churn, NRR 118%. SMB: Inkwell's $9 plan has cut Palisade's win rate from 51% to 38%.
The CFO's $10.3M is really ~$4.2M, and the extra $1.2M over our plan depends on SMB

Contracts not renewing in 2027 and the 7% enterprise cap cut it to $7.6M; churn cuts it to $4.2M. Our plan gives $3.0M. If customers are more price-sensitive than we assume, both give ~$2.0M, so the flat 12% buys upside only if Inkwell has not changed SMB behaviour.
Raise in January, gate SMB on a test, and plan for new customers to close the 15% gap

ARR reaches ~$97.0M (+12.8%) before new customers; NRR stays ~113%. Mid-market and enterprise rises start at January renewals. An SMB test runs in Q1–Q2, with an H2 rise only if it passes. Churn triggers can pause any step.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis.

slides.title: We started with 'raise by segment, including a modest SMB rise'; the evidence supported raising mid-market and enterprise, but not SMB yet

paragraphs.text: We started with 'raise by segment, including a modest SMB rise'; the evidence supported raising mid-market and enterprise, but not SMB yet

Initial hypothesis (stated before testing): Raise prices in 2027, but vary the rise by segment: about +10% for mid-market and enterprise and +8% for SMB (the size of the 2023 rise), with no rise for the promo cohort.

data: What would have to be true
H1. Rising churn does not reflect a general reaction against the price
Core SMB churn 2.0% → 2.1%; share citing price 19% → 18% for this group. The promo cohort churns at ~4.9%: it is 36% of SMB customers but 56% of SMB churners. Mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%, enterprise flat.
H2a. Mid-market and enterprise can absorb a rise without churn wiping out the gain

Mid-market +10% test: conversion 23.1% vs 23.6%, not significant. Churn ≤0.8% a month, NRR 112–118%. Customers stay for integrations and the audit trail. Inkwell not seen in deals over 200 seats. Caveat: the test was on new sign-ups, not renewals.
H2b. Core SMB can absorb +8% as it did in 2023

In 2023, +8% added 0.5pp to monthly churn for 6 months and the rise still paid off. Since then, Inkwell launched at $9 against our $15 and the SMB win rate fell from 51% to 38%. We have no data on how renewing SMB customers react to price after Inkwell.
Not proven: revised to test first
H3. The rise is big enough to matter for the 2027 targets
It is worth $3.0–4.2M net, not $10.3M. NRR stays above 100% in every option. No option reaches +15% without new customers.
H4. The downside can be seen early and limited
Prices change only at renewal, so the effect shows up month by month. Break-even churn levels are known for each segment. A test design worked in 2024.

paragraphs.text: What changed: The SMB rise moved from 'raise in January' to 'test now, decide by end of Q2'. The value estimate fell from the $10.3M headline to $3–4M net.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis.

Churn is rising because of the 2025 promotion cohort: core SMB and enterprise churn are flat, and mid-market is up only 0.2pp
Monthly logo churn, % of customers
What this means
•  Core SMB churn has barely moved: 2.0% → 2.1%. The share of these churners citing price fell from 19% to 18%, so Inkwell has not yet hurt retention.
•  The promo cohort drives the rise: 36% of SMB customers but 56% of SMB churners. 103 of the 183 SMB customers lost each month come from it.
•  The rise should fade as this cohort leaves the base. If they churned like other SMB customers, SMB churn would be 2.1%, not 3.1%.
•  Mid-market churn is slightly up (0.6% → 0.8%) and the pack does not explain it. We watch it as a guardrail metric.
joined Feb–Aug 2025
Promo-cohort churn is derived: (5,900 × 3.1% − 3,800 × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100 = 4.9% a month. This uses mid-2026 customer counts for H1 rates, so treat it as approximate.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis.

data: Mostly within 2 months of the discount ending

paragraphs.text: Implications for the two internal claims
•  CFO, 'onboarding, not price': half right. Core customers are not leaving over price, but the promo cohort is: they left when their price doubled.

•  Customer Success, 'halve SMB churn in two quarters': not credible. Halving it means 1.55%, below the 2.1% of customers who were onboarded normally. Full activation is worth ~$0.3M of ARR in 2027. Even churn at the core rate would save only ~$1.0M.
•  So: no rise for the promo cohort, retention work for it, and no more 50%-off acquisition offers.

Method: customers who send <5 documents in month 1 churn ~3× as often as those who send more. Fitting the core mix (72% activated) to 2.1% gives activated churn of 1.35%. The promo mix (41% activated) then predicts 2.9%; the actual is 4.9%.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis.

Why this matters
•  Inkwell launched in October 2025, yet core SMB churn in H1 2026 was flat and price was cited by only 18% of churners. Existing customers are staying.
•  The pressure is on winning new customers: Palisade lost 13 points of win rate in Inkwell deals.
•  The 15% target needs $0.7–1.9M of net new-customer ARR under either price-rise option, and SMB is where Inkwell competes.
•  How price-sensitive SMB customers now are is the main uncertainty in the pack. Test it before rolling it out.
Palisade costs 1.67× Inkwell today, 1.80× after +8% and 1.87× after +12%. Business plan $29 vs Inkwell Pro $24.

slides.title: A rise pays while the churn it causes stays below p/(1+p): mid-market and enterprise clear this easily, core SMB narrowly, the promo cohort not at all

paragraphs.text: 1  Diagnosis
2  Pricing power
3  Value
4  Plan
A rise pays while the churn it causes stays below p/(1+p): mid-market and enterprise clear this easily, core SMB narrowly, the promo cohort not at all
Extra ARR lost to the rise, % of renewing ARR, compared with break-even
Reading the chart
•  Break-even: a rise of p gains p on customers who stay and loses (1+p) on each extra one who leaves. It pays while extra churn < p/(1+p): 9.1% at +10%, 10.7% at +12%.
•  Mid-market and enterprise: the estimate is 2.1% at +10%, a quarter of break-even. Even at SMB-level sensitivity (4.5%) the rise pays.
•  Core SMB: fine at 2023 sensitivity. At twice that, the downside if Inkwell has changed behaviour, +12% loses money and +8% roughly breaks even.
•  Promo cohort: loses money even in the base case.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis.

What has to be true
•  Trailing NRR holds in 2027 (SMB 94%, mid-market 112%, enterprise 118%), giving +$8.0M. This is the biggest assumption in the bridge.
•  Price adds $3.0M net (downside $2.0M); the SMB gate could add up to $0.5M.
•  New-customer ARR of ≥$1.9M net of churn by December. The pack has no pipeline data, so Sales must confirm this.
•  For comparison: the CFO's plan reaches $98.2M and still needs $0.7M from new customers.

slides.title: Appendix A1: Net gain = renewing ARR × retention × (price rise − churn caused by the rise), calibrated on the 2023 and 2024 price evidence

paragraphs.text: Appendix A1: Net gain = renewing ARR × retention × (price rise − churn caused by the rise), calibrated on the 2023 and 2024 price evidence
•  Net gain per segment = R × g × [p − c × (1 + p)]
–  R = ARR renewing in 2027: SMB 100% of $21.0M; mid-market 85% of $41.0M = $34.85M; enterprise 40% of $24.0M = $9.6M
–  g = share retained over 12 months at the H1 2026 monthly churn rate, (1 − m)^12
–  p = price rise; enterprise capped portion (60%) limited to 7%
–  c = extra share of retained ARR lost because of the rise; break-even when c = p/(1+p)
•  Sensitivity (c per point of price)
–  SMB 0.45%: 2023 +8% added 0.5pp churn for 6 months and 0.1pp for the next 6 = 3.6% ÷ 8
–  Mid-market and enterprise 0.21%: 2024 test conversion 23.1% vs 23.6% = 2.1% relative ÷ 10
–  Promo cohort: SMB × 2.9 (52% ÷ 18% citing price)
–  Downside: mid-market and enterprise at SMB sensitivity; core SMB ×2; promo ×1.5
•  Simplifications
–  All repricing measured as a December 2027 run-rate, regardless of renewal month; this overstates revenue booked within 2027
–  Effect of the price rise on new-customer conversion not modelled (no SMB data)

slides.title: Appendix A2: The board dashboard's 'monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%' does not match any weighting of the segment data; restate it

paragraphs.text: Appendix A2: The board dashboard's 'monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%' does not match any weighting of the segment data; restate it

data: Logo churn, weighted by customers, excluding promo cohort

paragraphs.text: Recommendation
•  Report churn separately by segment and by cohort (promo vs core), as both logo churn and gross revenue churn, each with a written definition.
•  Weighted by customers, SMB dominates the blended figure (80% of customers but 24% of ARR). Weighted by ARR, churn is about 1.2% a month, a much less alarming picture for the board.
•  Until the metric is restated, the board's '2.3%' should not be used to judge the price decision.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis.
